The *Uḷāravimānavatthu* (Vv 29) is a short poetic narrative belonging to the *Vimānavatthu* collection in the Pali Canon [SuttaCentral]. The text recounts the story of a celestial being (*deva*) who explains the great heavenly splendor and happiness attained in the divine realm as the karmic result of offering a single oil cake to the Arahant Moggallāna [SuttaCentral]. Five translations into five modern languages are cataloged on SuttaCentral, including the English rendering "Splendid Mansion" by Bhikkhu Sujato [SuttaCentral].

No formal parallels in other Buddhist traditions are curated by SuttaCentral [SuttaCentral]. Automatically computed text-reuse analysis via DharmaNexus indicates extensive internal Pali reuse with the commentary *Vimānavatthu-aṭṭhakathā* (52 matching units, spanning segments §4.1–10.3) [DharmaNexus]. Furthermore, recurring stock verses and formulaic expressions are shared with several other texts in the *Vimānavatthu*, notably the *Guttilavimānavatthu* (Vv 33), *Daddallavimānavatthu* (Vv 34), *Dutiyasūcivimānavatthu* (Vv 59), and *Ambavimānavatthu* (Vv 46) [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also aligns isolated phrases with the Chinese *Saṃyuktāgama* (T 99) and the Tibetan *Vimaladattāparipṛcchāsūtra* (D 77), although these reflect machine matches of generic formulaic phrasing rather than established textual parallels [DharmaNexus].
